name: Antigravity CLI
description: Gives Google's Antigravity CLI (agy) an Antigravity plugin of Polter's own, ~/.gemini/config/plugins/polter: Polter's MCP server, its skills, its rules note and its hooks, all inside that one directory. None of your own files under ~/.gemini is edited, and Gemini CLI's are not touched. Antigravity asks before every call to one of Polter's tools, and nothing Polter can write into its plugin stops that, so a role starts agy with --dangerously-skip-permissions unless it says otherwise: no tool asks any more, shell commands included. To confirm each one, set the role's "Skip permissions" launch option to ask; then choose "always allow" in the box for Polter's tools, and Antigravity writes that into your own settings.json and does not ask again.

blocks: Do you trust the contents of this project?

skills.title: Install skills as well
skills.description: yes mirrors Polter's skills into this host's skills directory. Polter's skill_read has to be thought of first; a host's own skills are matched against what the user asked for, which is the whole difference. no registers the MCP server and nothing else.

rules.title: Write Polter's note into this CLI's rules file
rules.description: yes writes a marked block into the rules file of Polter's Antigravity plugin (never a file of yours or a project's) saying that what an agent prints reaches nobody, and pointing at the operating-a-terminal skill. It is there because a skill is matched against what the user asked for and nothing matches "you have just finished a task": on real records, 71 tasks produced 15 done reports. no takes the block, and the file, back out.

hooks.title: Let Polter hear what Antigravity is doing
hooks.description: yes writes Polter's hooks into its Antigravity plugin (~/.gemini/config/plugins/polter/hooks.json): they tell Polter when a session starts, a turn begins and ends, and a tool runs, so a supervisor sees a finished turn without waiting for the screen to go still. Antigravity loads its plugins for every session, so they also run in an agy you start yourself; outside Polter they do nothing. no takes them back out.
